lines.text: A polar bear's skin is black.
And its fur isn't even white. Wait for the last part.
See that black nose? The same dark skin covers its whole body.
Each hair is clear, with no pigment, and hollow inside.
Like snow and ice, the hairs scatter sunlight, so the coat looks white.
And the fur holds heat so well, on a heat camera the bear almost disappears.
Sounds fake? It's true. Follow for more.
